newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S COSATU REJECTS WAGE MODERATION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S COSATU REJECTS WAGE MODERATION.

text.p: A top Congress of South African Trade Unions' (Cosatu) official said on Saturday the federation was not prepared to moderate its wage demands.

Connie September, the federation's second vice-president, told reporters after a top-level executive meeting at the weekend that workers were still struggling to acquire basic needs like housing and electricity, and could not afford cuts.
"It would be a futile exercise for the federation to go in and discuss wage moderation against the backdrop of a number of key things that our members require.
"I think the old apartheid wage gap is still very much alive, and that's the key thing that needs to be targetted in that kind of discussion," she said.
September added workers would continue to demand improved wages for as long as income distribution was balanced in favour of the wealthy.

"You will ask for a revolution if you ask me (as a worker) to cut my wages that I got the other day through a strike, versus the number of basic needs that the country and workers still require," she said.
